descriptions.text: SiloFinance's pre-release leverage contract LeverageUsingSiloFlashloanWithGeneralSwap contained an arbitrary external call vulnerability in its openLeveragePosition function. The function accepted user-controlled _swapArgs without any validation, allowing an attacker to embed malicious parameters that designated the attacker's own address as the token receiver while specifying a victim address (which had granted maximum allowance to the contract) as the borrower. The contract then called silo.borrow() on the victim's behalf and transferred borrowed assets directly to the attacker, draining approximately $552,000 in ETH. Core Silo vaults and markets were isolated from the exploit. Attack Tx: 0x8e8dbc6b975dd664f1610f36c1e1990822ff142aa54129c28f39c7506bad091b Analysis: BlockSec Team Alert

According to Silo Labs' postmortem report, an unreleased leverage feature smart contract deployed on Ethereum mainnet and Sonic was exploited during its testing phase. The affected contract was separate from Silo’s core infrastructure. The attacker manipulated the _swapArgs parameter within the contract to execute unauthorized borrowing, leveraging user approvals granted during testing. The exploit resulted in a loss of 224 ETH, which belonged to SiloDAO. No user funds were at risk, as the feature had not yet been made public.

On June 25, 2025, Silo Finance lost $545,000 in Ethereum after an attacker exploited an unreleased leverage contract on mainnet. The contract trusted user-supplied call targets and data, allowing malicious borrowing calls that drained only DAO test funds. Core protocol, vaults, and user markets were unaffected. The leverage contract's openLeveragePosition function forwarded user-supplied call data and contract addresses without validation. This allowed an attacker to invoke borrow operations on real Silo markets, causing unauthorized transfers from the DAO's accounts.
